version.changelog: Add generate_image.py script, refactor to script-based execution

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ai-image-gen
Version: 1.1.0

The skill defaults to a third-party API proxy (code.newcli.com) and promotes a specific commercial service via an affiliate link in the README (foxcode.rjj.cc). This architecture encourages users to provide their API keys to non-official endpoints, posing a risk of credential harvesting by the proxy operator. While the Python script (scripts/generate_image.py) performs its stated function without obvious system-level malice, the redirection of sensitive credentials to third-party infrastructure is a significant security risk.

llm.summary: This image-generation skill does what it broadly claims, but it under-discloses sensitive API-key and prompt handling through configurable third-party endpoints and allows unrestricted local file output paths.

dimensions.detail: Network access, an API key, and file writes are expected for image generation, but the destination host is unrestricted and output paths can point anywhere writable by the running process.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The README shows a normal ClawHub install command and environment-variable setup; it also recommends a third-party registration link with an affiliate parameter, which users should review before use.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions disclose the IMAGE_GEN_API_KEY and IMAGE_GEN_BASE_URL variables, but do not clearly warn that prompts and credentials are sent to the configured endpoint, whose default is a third-party relay rather than an official provider URL.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background service, memory modification, or privilege escalation behavior was found; the main local mutation risk is caller-controlled file creation or overwrite.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is AI image generation and editing, but the shipped script only supports text-to-image generation; claims about image-plus-text generation, editing, and style conversion are broader than the implemented capability.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the provider endpoint before installing or running this skill. Use a narrowly scoped, revocable API key, avoid sensitive prompts, and do not let untrusted requests choose the output path. Treat the editing and image-to-image claims as unsupported unless the package is updated with clear implementation and scoping.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Supported by artifact evidence: SKILL.md advertises image editing, image-plus-text generation, and style conversion, while scripts/generate_image.py only accepts a text prompt and sends it to an image-generation endpoint.
[LP3] expected: Partly supported: environment access, network calls, and file output fit the image-generation purpose, but the artifacts do not provide a tight permissions boundary or clear host/output scoping.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-only documentation is visible to users and not hidden behavior; this is a usability and disclosure note rather than a primary security concern.
[T09] unexpected: Supported in context: the script sends IMAGE_GEN_API_KEY and full prompt content to a configurable BASE_URL with no destination validation, including a third-party default endpoint.
[T09] unexpected: Supported in context: the --output argument is written directly with Path.write_bytes, so a caller-controlled path can overwrite any file writable by the process.
